findings.summary: The sole named acceptance criterion for M0.7 -- the base-ref step 'FAILS rather than defaulting to a range that examines nothing' -- still has zero automated test in this commit, and the three mutations I demonstrated in round one (`exit 1`->`|| true`; deleting the `git cat-file -e` check; `*) base=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)`->`*) base=HEAD`) still survive silently against the tree today. What changed since round one is that the M0.26 row is now genuinely present and quotes those three mutations verbatim, so the gap is tracked with enough detail that closing it does not require re-deriving anything. I accept the deferral: this project already closes a task 'done' while spinning an identified, zero-coverage residual into its own row rather than blocking indefinitely -- M0.29 shipped with M0.30 carrying its residual hardening, M0.31 shipped with M0.32/M0.33 carrying its residual gaps including M0.33's own admission that 'the one-line fix has no regression coverage.' M0.7/M0.26 is the same shape, not a new exception. Extracting and testing here, as the author notes, is exactly what the production reviewer already flagged as scope creep on this same task; repeating that argument in round two of the test review would manufacture the round-3 thrash rule 12 exists to prevent, over a task whose current correctness was independently verified by hand (six scenarios, round one) rather than merely assumed.
findings.failure_scenario: Between now and whenever M0.26 lands, an edit to lines 66-79 that reintroduces any of the three named mutations passes every gate in this repository and both review lenses silently, because nothing executes ci.yml and nothing executes an extracted equivalent of it. The exposure is bounded by M0.26 existing as a concretely-scoped, non-vague task -- if that row is deprioritized or reworded to drop the three mutations, this becomes a real regression risk with no tracking, and a future test-reviewer would be right to make it blocking at that point.

answer_to_author: Accept the deferral, on the strength of precedent already in this backlog rather than as a new carve-out. M0.29->M0.30 and M0.31->M0.32/M0.33 establish that this project closes a task 'done' while spinning a named, zero-coverage residual into its own row, provided the row preserves enough detail to act on without re-deriving it -- M0.26 now does, verbatim, for all three mutations. Forcing the extraction into this commit would be the exact scope creep the production reviewer already flagged on this task, and doing it anyway in round two to satisfy the test review would be round-2-blocking for a reason the process itself provides a sanctioned escape hatch for. The one condition I'd hold you to: if M0.26 slips past the current milestone without landing, re-open this as major -- the precedent rows (M0.30, M0.32, M0.33) are all still 'todo' too, and 'tracked' is not the same claim as 'closed soon.'
